The European Court of Human Rights ruled in 2001 (Grand Chamber, 21 November 2001) that there was no violation of Article 6(1). By a narrow 9–8 majority, it held that the UK's grant of state immunity to Kuwait in a civil suit over alleged torture pursued a legitimate aim and was proportionate. The Court reasoned that, at that time, international law did not yet recognize an exception to state immunity for civil claims over torture committed abroad.

CONFIDENCE: 96
